name: WebResearchSummarizer
description: Searches the web for information on a given topic and synthesizes findings into a coherent cited summary. Handles multi-source aggregation, contradiction resolution, and relevance filtering.
triggerConditions: User wants information from multiple web sources
User asks about current events or recent developments
User requests topic research without providing source documents
examples: Research the latest advancements in solid-state batteries
Summarize analyst opinions on the EV market in 2025
What are the latest developments in AI regulation?
limitations: Not intended for academic literature reviews — use AcademicPaperAnalyzer
Should not be used when documents are already provided by the user
Cannot access private or internal company knowledge

name: AcademicPaperAnalyzer
description: Reads and analyzes academic papers (PDFs or URLs), extracting methodology, findings, limitations, and contribution to the field. Can compare multiple papers and identify research gaps.
triggerConditions: User uploads or links to a research paper and wants analysis
User wants to understand the methodology or conclusions of a study
User is conducting a literature review
examples: Analyze this paper and tell me its main contributions and weaknesses
Compare these two papers on transformer architectures
What methodology does this study use and is it statistically sound?
limitations: Not for general web research — use WebResearchSummarizer
Does not perform statistical re-analysis of raw data
Should not be selected for summarizing blog posts or news articles
skillBody: Extract abstract, methodology, findings, and limitations
Compare across multiple papers if provided
Highlight research gaps and future work suggestions

name: CompetitorIntelligenceGatherer
description: Researches and profiles competitor companies by aggregating public information including product offerings, pricing, recent news, leadership, and strategic direction. Produces structured competitive analysis reports.
triggerConditions: User wants to understand a competitor's positioning or strategy
User is preparing a competitive analysis or market map
User asks how a company's products compare to others in the market
examples: Give me a competitive breakdown of Salesforce vs HubSpot for SMBs
What are Notion's main weaknesses compared to Confluence?
Research our top 3 competitors and summarize their go-to-market strategies
limitations: Cannot access paywalled financial filings or private company data
Not suitable for deep technical product benchmarking
Should not replace dedicated market research platforms
skillBody: Aggregate public information on products and pricing
Summarize recent news and strategic moves
Compare feature sets and market positioning

name: FactChecker
description: Verifies specific factual claims by cross-referencing multiple authoritative sources. Flags unsupported, contested, or false claims and provides sourced corrections or confirmations.
triggerConditions: User wants to verify whether a specific claim is true
User needs to fact-check content before publishing
User expresses doubt about a statistic or assertion
examples: Is it true that Python is the most used programming language in 2024?
Fact-check this paragraph from our press release
Verify this statistic: 70% of startups fail in the first year
limitations: Not designed for broad research — focuses on specific claim verification
Cannot verify internal or proprietary company claims
Should not be used for legal or medical verification requiring licensed professionals
skillBody: Parse and isolate individual factual claims
Classify each claim as supported, contested, or false

name: CalendarEventScheduler
description: Creates, modifies, and deletes calendar events on connected calendar services (Google Calendar, Outlook). Handles time zone resolution, recurrence rules, attendee invites, and conflict detection.
triggerConditions: User wants to schedule a meeting or event
User asks to block time on their calendar
User wants to set a recurring reminder or appointment
examples: Schedule a 1-hour team standup every Monday at 9am
Block my calendar next Friday afternoon for deep work
Create a meeting with john@example.com for Tuesday at 3pm EST
limitations: Requires calendar integration to be connected
Does not find optimal meeting windows across attendees — use MeetingOptimizer
Not suitable for building meeting agendas — use MeetingAgendaBuilder
skillBody: Create or update the event via calendar API

name: MeetingOptimizer
description: Analyzes calendars of multiple participants to find optimal meeting windows, considering time zones, working hours, existing commitments, and stated preferences. Suggests ranked time slots.
triggerConditions: User wants to find a meeting time that works for multiple people
User is coordinating across time zones and needs scheduling assistance
User asks when everyone on a team is free
examples: Find a time for a 30-minute call with Alice in London and Bob in Tokyo this week
When can our whole team meet next week? Everyone's calendar is connected
What's the best time for a bi-weekly sync between NYC and SF teams?
limitations: Requires access to all participants' calendars
Does not create the event — use CalendarEventScheduler for that
Cannot account for informal preferences not reflected in calendar data
skillBody: Fetch calendar availability for all participants
Rank slots by quality (fewest conflicts, best hours)

name: TaskManager
description: Creates, updates, assigns, prioritizes, and closes tasks in connected task management tools (Todoist, Asana, Jira, Linear, Notion). Supports natural language task creation with due dates, priorities, and tags.
triggerConditions: User wants to add, edit, or complete a task or to-do item
User asks to create action items from a conversation
User wants to view or update their task list
examples: Add a task to review the Q3 report by Friday with high priority
Mark the onboarding checklist task as done
Create tasks from the action items in this meeting notes document
limitations: Not for project-level planning — use ProjectPlanGenerator
Cannot manage tasks in disconnected tools
Should not be selected for calendar events or reminders
skillBody: Parse task details from natural language
Extract due dates, priorities, and assignees
Create or update tasks in connected tool
Confirm task creation or update to user

name: EmailDraftComposer
description: Composes professional email drafts based on user intent, context, and tone preferences. Handles cold outreach, follow-ups, meeting requests, feedback delivery, apologies, and formal correspondence.
triggerConditions: User wants to write or draft an email
User describes a situation and asks for help responding via email
User needs to communicate something formally in writing
examples: Write a follow-up email to a client who hasn't responded in two weeks
Draft a polite rejection email for a job applicant
Compose a cold outreach email to a potential enterprise customer
limitations: Does not send emails — use EmailSender for delivery
Not designed for internal Slack or chat messages — use SlackMessageComposer
Should not be used for legal notices requiring attorney review
skillBody: Draft subject line and email body
Return polished draft for user review

name: EmailSender
description: Sends emails through connected email accounts (Gmail, Outlook). Can use drafted content or compose and send in one step. Supports CC/BCC, attachments, reply threading, and scheduled sending.
triggerConditions: User explicitly asks to send an email
User approves a draft and wants it delivered
User wants to schedule an email for a specific send time
examples: Send this draft to the team now
Email the proposal to client@company.com with the attached PDF
Schedule this email to go out Monday morning at 8am
limitations: Requires a connected email account
Should not be used to only draft content — use EmailDraftComposer
Cannot send to distribution lists without proper permissions
skillBody: Send via connected email provider and confirm

name: SlackMessageComposer
description: Drafts and optionally sends Slack messages including channel posts, direct messages, and threaded replies. Adapts tone to informal workplace communication and formats with Slack markdown.
triggerConditions: User wants to write a Slack message or announcement
User wants to reply to a Slack thread
User asks for help communicating something informally to colleagues
examples: Write a Slack announcement for our product launch tomorrow
Draft a DM to my manager asking for time off next week
Post a team update in #engineering about the deployment
limitations: Not for formal email communication — use EmailDraftComposer
Sending requires Slack integration to be connected
Not suitable for long-form documents or reports
skillBody: Adapt tone for workplace chat context
Send via Slack API if connected and confirmed

name: MeetingNotesTranscriber
description: Processes meeting transcripts or recordings and produces structured notes including summary, key decisions, action items with owners, open questions, and next steps.
triggerConditions: User provides a meeting transcript and wants it processed
User uploads a recording or transcript file
User asks for action items or a summary from a meeting
examples: Summarize this meeting transcript and extract all action items
Turn this Zoom transcript into structured meeting notes
Who owns what from this meeting? Extract action items with owners
limitations: Requires transcript or recording input — cannot attend live meetings
Does not send meeting notes — use EmailSender or SlackMessageComposer
Not appropriate for generating pre-meeting agendas — use MeetingAgendaBuilder
skillBody: Ingest and parse transcript or audio
List action items with owners and due dates
Summarize open questions and next steps

name: MeetingAgendaBuilder
description: Creates structured meeting agendas based on meeting purpose, attendees, duration, and prior context. Suggests time allocations for each agenda item, pre-read materials, and facilitator notes.
triggerConditions: User wants to prepare an agenda before a meeting
User asks what topics to cover in an upcoming meeting
User is planning a workshop or structured session
examples: Build an agenda for a 60-minute quarterly planning meeting with leadership
Create a structured agenda for a project kickoff with a new client
What should we cover in tomorrow's product review? Generate an agenda
limitations: Does not produce post-meeting notes — use MeetingNotesTranscriber
Not for scheduling the meeting itself — use CalendarEventScheduler
Should not be selected for general document creation
skillBody: Propose agenda items based on purpose and attendees
Add facilitator tips and pre-read suggestions
Format as a structured agenda document

name: GitHubIssueReader
description: Fetches and reads GitHub issues from a specified repository. Retrieves issue details, comments, labels, assignees, linked PRs, and status. Supports filtering by label, milestone, assignee, or state.
triggerConditions: User wants to read or view existing GitHub issues
User asks what issues are open in a repository
User wants to understand the details of a specific GitHub issue
examples: Show me all open bugs labeled 'critical' in the backend repo
What's the current status of issue #452?
List all issues assigned to me in the frontend repository
limitations: Cannot create or modify issues — use GitHubIssueCreator
Requires GitHub integration and appropriate repository access
Not suitable for reading pull requests — use GitHubPRReviewer

name: GitHubIssueCreator
description: Creates new GitHub issues in a specified repository. Supports setting title, body, labels, assignees, milestone, and project associations. Can generate issue content from user descriptions or bug reports.
triggerConditions: User wants to file a new GitHub issue
User describes a bug or feature request to be tracked
User asks to create a ticket from a conversation or document
examples: Create a GitHub issue for the login page crash on Safari
File a feature request issue for dark mode support in the mobile app
Turn these 3 bugs from the QA report into GitHub issues
limitations: Cannot read or update existing issues — use GitHubIssueReader
Requires write access to the target repository
Not for pull request creation
skillBody: Parse issue title and description from input

name: GitHubPRReviewer
description: Analyzes GitHub pull requests including code diffs, commit history, and review comments. Provides structured feedback on code quality, logic errors, test coverage, and adherence to conventions. Can summarize PR changes.
triggerConditions: User wants to review a pull request
User asks for feedback on code changes in a PR
User wants a plain-language summary of what a PR does
examples: Review PR #88 and flag any potential bugs
Summarize what changes PR #201 introduces to the auth module
Give me feedback on this PR diff before I merge it
limitations: Cannot merge or close PRs — requires separate user action
Not for creating issues — use GitHubIssueCreator
Should not be selected for repository-level analysis — use GitHubRepoAnalyzer
skillBody: Fetch PR diff and commit history
Analyze code changes for bugs and style issues
Summarize overall PR changes in plain language

name: GitHubRepoAnalyzer
description: Performs high-level analysis of a GitHub repository including codebase structure, tech stack, contributor activity, open issue and PR volume, test coverage trends, and dependency health. Produces an architectural overview.
triggerConditions: User wants an overview or audit of an entire repository
User is onboarding to a new codebase and wants to understand its structure
User wants to assess the health or activity of a GitHub project
examples: Give me an overview of this open-source repo before I contribute
Analyze the dependency health of our main backend repository
What are the most active areas of this codebase in the last 90 days?
limitations: Not for reviewing individual PRs — use GitHubPRReviewer
Not for reading specific issues — use GitHubIssueReader
Requires repository access; may be limited on private repos
skillBody: Map directory structure and tech stack
Analyze contributor activity and commit cadence
Assess dependency versions and known vulnerabilities
Produce a structured repository health report

name: CodeDebugger
description: Analyzes provided code snippets or files to identify bugs, logic errors, runtime exceptions, and edge case failures. Explains root causes and provides corrected code. Supports multiple programming languages.
triggerConditions: User shares code and reports an error or unexpected behavior
User pastes a stack trace and asks what is wrong
User says their code is not working as expected
examples: This Python function throws a KeyError — can you find the bug?
My React component re-renders infinitely. What's causing it?
Debug this SQL query that returns duplicate rows
limitations: Cannot run or execute code — use CodeExecutor for that
Not designed for generating new code from scratch — use CodeGenerator
Should not be selected for PR review workflows — use GitHubPRReviewer
skillBody: Parse and understand the code structure
Trace execution path for the reported error
Identify root cause of the bug

name: CodeGenerator
description: Generates new code from natural language specifications. Supports functions, classes, APIs, scripts, and boilerplate across multiple programming languages and frameworks. Applies best practices and includes inline documentation.
triggerConditions: User asks to write a new function, script, or component
User describes desired behavior and wants working code produced
User needs boilerplate or starter code for a task
examples: Write a Python function to parse nested JSON and flatten it
Generate a REST API endpoint in FastAPI for user registration
Create a React component for a responsive navbar with a hamburger menu
limitations: Not for debugging existing code — use CodeDebugger
Does not execute or test the generated code — use CodeExecutor
Not appropriate for explaining existing code — use CodeExplainer

name: CodeExplainer
description: Reads and explains existing code in plain language. Describes what a function, module, or file does, identifies design patterns used, and maps dependencies. Useful for onboarding, documentation, and code review.
triggerConditions: User shares code and asks what it does
User wants a plain-language explanation of a function or module
User is trying to understand an unfamiliar codebase section
examples: Explain what this middleware function does line by line
What design pattern is used in this class?
Walk me through this authentication module in simple terms
limitations: Not for fixing bugs — use CodeDebugger
Not for generating new code — use CodeGenerator
Should not be used for full repository analysis — use GitHubRepoAnalyzer
skillBody: Parse and tokenize the provided code
Identify language, framework, and design patterns
Map data flow and control flow
Return a structured explanation with annotations

name: CodeExecutor
description: Executes code snippets in a sandboxed environment and returns output, errors, or computed results. Supports Python, JavaScript, and Bash. Useful for verifying logic, running data transformations, or quick computations.
triggerConditions: User explicitly wants code to be run or executed
User wants to verify the output of a script
User needs to compute something programmatically
examples: Run this Python script and show me the output
Execute this data transformation and return the result
Test if this sorting algorithm works correctly on this input
limitations: Sandboxed environment — no external network access or persistent file system
Not for code generation — use CodeGenerator
Not for debugging without execution context — use CodeDebugger
skillBody: Run the code with provided inputs
Capture stdout, stderr, and return values
Return formatted output or error trace

name: PDFReader
description: Extracts and processes text, tables, and metadata from PDF files. Supports scanned PDFs via OCR, multi-page navigation, and section extraction. Enables downstream Q&A, summarization, or data extraction from PDF content.
triggerConditions: User uploads a PDF and wants to read or extract content from it
User asks questions about the contents of a PDF
User needs to parse tables or text from a PDF document
examples: What are the main conclusions in this PDF report?
Extract all the financial figures from this PDF into a table
Summarize pages 5 through 12 of this contract PDF
limitations: Cannot modify or fill PDF forms — use PDFFormFiller
Cannot generate new PDFs — use PDFGenerator
Complex image-heavy PDFs may have extraction accuracy issues
skillBody: Apply OCR if document is scanned
Extract text and tables by page or section
Return structured content for downstream use

name: PDFGenerator
description: Creates new PDF documents from provided content, templates, or structured data. Supports custom layouts, headers, footers, tables, charts, and branding. Can convert HTML, Markdown, or Word content into PDF.
triggerConditions: User wants to create or export a document as a PDF
User asks to generate a PDF report, invoice, or certificate
User wants to convert existing content into a PDF file
examples: Generate a branded PDF report from this Markdown content
Create a PDF invoice for this order summary
Export this proposal as a formatted PDF with our company logo
limitations: Cannot read or extract content from existing PDFs — use PDFReader
Cannot fill interactive form fields in existing PDFs — use PDFFormFiller
Not for editing existing PDF files
skillBody: Add headers, footers, and page numbers

name: PDFFormFiller
description: Fills out interactive form fields in existing PDF documents using provided data. Supports text fields, checkboxes, dropdowns, and signature fields. Can auto-populate forms from structured data sources.
triggerConditions: User has a PDF with form fields to fill out
User wants to populate a standard form with their data
User asks to auto-fill a PDF template with known field values
examples: Fill in this W-9 PDF form with the contractor's details
Auto-populate this vendor onboarding PDF with data from our CRM
Complete the fields in this NDA PDF template with the provided info
limitations: Only works on PDFs with interactive form fields — not flat PDFs
Cannot create a new PDF from scratch — use PDFGenerator
Cannot extract general text for reading — use PDFReader
skillBody: Detect and list interactive form fields
Map input data to field names
Fill text fields, checkboxes, and dropdowns

name: SpreadsheetAnalyzer
description: Reads and analyzes spreadsheet data (Excel, CSV, Google Sheets) to produce summaries, detect patterns, compute statistics, and answer questions about the data. Handles formulas, pivot-like aggregations, and cross-tab analysis.
triggerConditions: User uploads a spreadsheet and wants to understand or analyze the data
User asks statistical or aggregation questions about tabular data
User wants to find patterns, outliers, or trends in a data file
examples: Analyze this sales CSV and tell me which region performed best
Find any outliers in this employee expense spreadsheet
Summarize the key trends in this monthly revenue Excel file
limitations: Not for generating charts or visualizations — use DataVisualizer
Cannot edit or write back to the spreadsheet — use SpreadsheetEditor
Not appropriate for SQL database queries — use SQLQueryRunner

name: SpreadsheetEditor
description: Modifies spreadsheet files (Excel, Google Sheets, CSV) by adding, updating, or deleting rows, columns, formulas, and formatting. Supports bulk operations, data transformations, and template population.
triggerConditions: User wants to make changes to a spreadsheet file
User wants to add data, update values, or apply formulas
User wants to clean or reformat spreadsheet data
examples: Add a Total column to this spreadsheet that sums each row
Clean this CSV by removing duplicates and standardizing date formats
Update Q4 actuals in this financial model spreadsheet
limitations: Not for reading or analyzing data — use SpreadsheetAnalyzer
Not for generating charts — use DataVisualizer
Requires file access or integration to write changes back
skillBody: Apply row, column, or formula modifications
Perform data cleaning operations if needed
Save and return the modified spreadsheet

name: DataVisualizer
description: Creates charts, graphs, and dashboards from structured data. Supports bar, line, pie, scatter, heatmap, and funnel charts. Accepts CSV, JSON, or spreadsheet input and produces embeddable or downloadable visuals.
triggerConditions: User wants to create a chart or graph from data
User asks to visualize trends or comparisons in a dataset
User wants a visual dashboard or graphical summary of data
examples: Create a bar chart comparing monthly sales by region
Visualize this time-series data as a line graph
Build a heatmap showing customer activity by hour and day of week
limitations: Not for data analysis or statistics — use SpreadsheetAnalyzer or SQLQueryRunner
Cannot connect to live data sources for interactive dashboards
Not for generating written reports — use ReportGenerator
skillBody: Determine appropriate chart type based on data shape
Apply axis labels, titles, and color schemes
Return downloadable or embeddable chart output

name: SQLQueryRunner
description: Writes and executes SQL queries against connected databases. Supports SELECT, aggregations, joins, subqueries, and window functions. Translates natural language questions into SQL and returns formatted results.
triggerConditions: User wants to query a connected database
User asks a data question that requires database access
User provides a natural language question about structured database data
examples: How many active users signed up in the last 30 days?
Write a SQL query to find the top 10 customers by lifetime value
Join the orders and customers tables to show orders with customer names
limitations: Requires a connected and accessible database
Does not perform data visualization — use DataVisualizer
Write operations (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) require explicit user confirmation
skillBody: Translate natural language to SQL if needed
Format results as a readable table

name: ReportGenerator
description: Produces structured written reports from data, research, or analysis inputs. Formats content with an executive summary, sections, findings, and recommendations. Supports business, technical, and analytical report types.
triggerConditions: User wants to produce a formal written report
User has data or findings and wants them formatted as a report
User asks for a structured document summarizing analysis or research
examples: Generate a monthly performance report from this data
Write a competitive analysis report based on this research
Produce an executive summary report of our Q3 results
limitations: Not for simple document creation — use WordDocumentCreator
Not for chart or visualization creation — use DataVisualizer
Should not be selected when the user only wants a data summary
skillBody: Organize input into sections (summary, findings, analysis, recommendations)
Write narrative prose for each section
Embed tables or figures if provided
Format and return the final report

name: WordDocumentCreator
description: Creates formatted Microsoft Word (.docx) documents from scratch. Supports headings, tables, bullet points, images, table of contents, headers, footers, and custom styling. Outputs professional documents from structured input.
triggerConditions: User wants to produce a Word document or .docx file
User asks for a downloadable document with rich formatting
User wants a professional template or structured Word file
examples: Create a Word document template for employee performance reviews
Generate a .docx proposal document from this outline
Make a formatted Word report with a table of contents and section headers
limitations: Not for PDFs — use PDFGenerator
Not for spreadsheets — use SpreadsheetEditor
Not for reading existing Word files — use DocumentReader
skillBody: Parse content structure and formatting requirements
Insert tables, bullet lists, and images
Generate table of contents if requested

name: DocumentReader
description: Reads and extracts content from uploaded documents including Word (.docx), plain text, and Markdown files. Enables Q&A, summarization, and content extraction from provided documents.
triggerConditions: User uploads a Word or text document and wants to understand its contents
User asks questions about the content of an uploaded document
User wants a summary or key points from a provided file
examples: What are the main points in this Word document?
Extract all action items from this uploaded report
Summarize this .docx contract in plain language
limitations: Cannot edit the document — use WordDocumentCreator or SpreadsheetEditor
Not for PDF reading — use PDFReader
Should not be selected for creating new documents from scratch
skillBody: Identify key points and action items

name: ResumeReviewer
description: Analyzes a resume for clarity, completeness, ATS compatibility, formatting, and impact of experience bullet points. Provides detailed feedback on how to improve the resume for a specific role or industry.
triggerConditions: User uploads their resume and wants feedback or improvement suggestions
User asks how to make their CV stronger
User wants to know if their resume is optimized for a specific role
examples: Review my resume and tell me what to improve
Is my resume ATS-friendly for software engineering roles?
Give me feedback on the bullet points in my experience section
limitations: Not for writing a resume from scratch
Not for matching resume to a JD — use JobDescriptionAnalyzer
Should not be selected for interview coaching — use InterviewPreparation
skillBody: Parse resume sections (summary, experience, education, skills)
Evaluate bullet point impact and clarity

name: InterviewPreparation
description: Helps candidates prepare for job interviews by generating likely questions, coaching on STAR-method answers, providing role-specific technical questions, and giving feedback on practice responses.
triggerConditions: User has an upcoming interview and wants to prepare
User asks for practice interview questions for a role
User wants feedback on their interview answer quality
examples: I have a product manager interview at Google — what questions should I prepare for?
Give me 10 behavioral interview questions for a senior engineer role
Evaluate my answer to this interview question and suggest improvements
limitations: Not for resume review — use ResumeReviewer
Not for analyzing job postings — use JobDescriptionAnalyzer
Not a substitute for actual mock interviews with human interviewers
skillBody: Generate relevant behavioral and technical questions
Coach on STAR method response structure
Return improvement tips and model answers

name: JobDescriptionAnalyzer
description: Analyzes job postings to extract required skills, responsibilities, compensation signals, culture indicators, and potential red flags. Can match a resume or candidate profile against a JD and score fit.
triggerConditions: User pastes or uploads a job description and wants it analyzed
User wants to understand what a specific role requires
User asks how well their background matches a job posting
examples: Analyze this job posting and tell me the top 5 required skills
How well does my resume match this job description?
Are there any red flags or unusual requirements in this JD?
limitations: Not for interview preparation — use InterviewPreparation
Not for reviewing a resume independently — use ResumeReviewer
Should not be selected for general company research
skillBody: Parse job description into structured sections
Score candidate fit if resume is provided

name: FinancialStatementAnalyzer
description: Analyzes financial statements (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow statement) to compute key ratios, identify trends, flag anomalies, and provide a structured financial health summary.
triggerConditions: User uploads or provides financial statements for analysis
User wants to understand a company's financial health or performance
User needs specific financial ratios computed from statements
examples: Analyze this company's income statement for the last 3 years
What is the debt-to-equity ratio from this balance sheet?
Identify any financial red flags in these quarterly statements
limitations: Not for financial forecasting — use FinancialForecaster
Not for personal budgeting — use BudgetPlanner
Does not provide investment advice
skillBody: Parse income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow data
Compute key financial ratios (P/E, ROE, debt-to-equity, etc.)

name: FinancialForecaster
description: Builds financial forecasts and projections using historical data and assumptions. Supports revenue forecasting, expense modeling, cash flow projection, and scenario analysis (base, bull, bear cases).
triggerConditions: User wants to project future financial performance
User provides historical financials and asks for a forecast
User wants to model different financial scenarios
examples: Project our revenue for the next 12 months based on current growth rate
Build a 3-year cash flow forecast with base and bear case scenarios
Model the financial impact of hiring 10 new engineers next quarter
limitations: Not for analyzing historical statements — use FinancialStatementAnalyzer
Not for personal budgeting — use BudgetPlanner
Forecasts are probabilistic estimates, not guarantees
skillBody: Build base, bull, and bear case models
Return formatted forecast with scenario comparison

name: BudgetPlanner
description: Helps individuals or teams plan and track budgets. Creates budget templates, allocates spending categories, tracks actuals vs. budget, and flags overspending. Supports personal finance and departmental budgeting.
triggerConditions: User wants to create or review a budget
User asks for help managing personal or team spending
User wants to track expenses against a budget
examples: Create a monthly personal budget based on my income of $6,000
Build a Q1 marketing department budget template
I'm overspending — help me identify where to cut in my budget
limitations: Not for forecasting business financials — use FinancialForecaster
Not for analyzing corporate financial statements — use FinancialStatementAnalyzer
Does not connect to bank accounts without explicit integration
skillBody: Return budget plan or variance summary

name: InvoiceProcessor
description: Extracts structured data from invoice PDFs or images including vendor, line items, amounts, tax, due dates, and payment terms. Can validate invoices against purchase orders and flag discrepancies.
triggerConditions: User uploads an invoice and needs data extracted
User wants to validate an invoice against a purchase order
User is processing invoices for accounting or accounts payable workflows
examples: Extract all line items and totals from this invoice PDF
Validate this invoice against our purchase order and flag mismatches
Process these 20 invoices and output a structured CSV of all data
limitations: Not for generating new invoices — use InvoiceGenerator
Not for general PDF reading — use PDFReader for non-invoice documents
Accuracy may decrease with handwritten or poorly scanned invoices
skillBody: Load invoice file and apply OCR if needed
Extract vendor, date, line items, taxes, and totals
Validate against purchase order if provided
Return structured invoice data or CSV

name: InvoiceGenerator
description: Creates professional invoices as PDFs or structured documents from provided billing data. Supports line items, tax calculations, payment terms, and branded templates. Can integrate with CRM or billing data sources.
triggerConditions: User wants to create an invoice to send to a client
User provides billing details and asks for an invoice to be generated
User needs a formatted invoice document or PDF
examples: Generate an invoice for $4,500 in consulting services for Acme Corp due in 30 days
Create a branded invoice from this project billing summary
Generate invoices for all completed orders in this spreadsheet
limitations: Not for processing or reading incoming invoices — use InvoiceProcessor
Does not submit invoices to payment processing systems
Not for general PDF creation — use PDFGenerator
skillBody: Calculate totals, taxes, and due dates
Render as PDF or structured document

name: ProjectPlanGenerator
description: Creates structured project plans with phases, milestones, tasks, dependencies, timelines, and resource assignments. Supports Gantt-style output and can initialize plans in connected project management tools.
triggerConditions: User wants to plan a new project from scratch
User asks for a project roadmap or work breakdown structure
User describes a goal and wants it decomposed into a structured project plan
examples: Create a project plan for a website redesign launching in 3 months
Build a work breakdown structure for a mobile app development project
Generate a Gantt chart plan for our product launch campaign
limitations: Not for individual task management — use TaskManager
Not for tracking ongoing project status — use ProjectStatusTracker
Should not be selected for meeting agendas — use MeetingAgendaBuilder
skillBody: Break goal into phases and deliverables
Export to connected project management tool

name: ProjectStatusTracker
description: Monitors and reports on project progress by querying connected project management tools. Produces status summaries showing completed tasks, blockers, at-risk milestones, and upcoming deadlines.
triggerConditions: User wants a status update on an ongoing project
User asks what has been completed or what is blocked
User needs a progress report for stakeholders
examples: What's the current status of the Q3 product launch project?
Which milestones are at risk this sprint?
Generate a weekly project status report for the engineering team
limitations: Requires connected project management tool with current data
Not for creating new project plans — use ProjectPlanGenerator
Not for individual task creation — use TaskManager
skillBody: Query connected PM tool for task and milestone data

name: RiskAssessor
description: Identifies, evaluates, and prioritizes project or business risks. Produces a risk register with likelihood, impact, mitigation strategies, and owners. Supports operational, financial, and technical risk types.
triggerConditions: User wants to identify risks in a project or business initiative
User asks for a risk register or risk analysis
User is preparing for a risk review meeting
examples: Identify the top risks for our cloud migration project
Create a risk register for our new product launch
What are the biggest operational risks of expanding to a new market?
limitations: Not for general project planning — use ProjectPlanGenerator
Not for financial forecasting — use FinancialForecaster
Does not replace professional risk assessment for regulated industries
skillBody: Identify risks from project or business context
Score each risk by likelihood and impact

name: KnowledgeBaseBuilder
description: Organizes and structures information into a searchable knowledge base. Ingests documents, notes, and URLs, extracts key concepts, and creates linked entries with tags and categories.
triggerConditions: User wants to build or populate an internal knowledge base
User has a collection of documents to organize into a structured resource
User wants to make institutional knowledge searchable
examples: Turn these 15 internal documents into a structured knowledge base
Build a searchable FAQ from these support tickets
Organize our onboarding materials into a tagged knowledge base
limitations: Not for querying an existing knowledge base — use KnowledgeBaseSearcher
Not for general document creation — use WordDocumentCreator
Should not be selected for summarizing a single document

name: KnowledgeBaseSearcher
description: Searches an existing connected knowledge base or document repository to answer specific questions. Uses semantic search to find the most relevant entries and surfaces cited answers.
triggerConditions: User asks a question that should be answered from internal documentation
User wants to find specific information in a company knowledge base
User asks 'do we have a doc on...' or similar
examples: What is our refund policy according to the internal docs?
Find documentation on how to configure SSO in our product
Search the knowledge base for anything related to GDPR compliance
limitations: Requires a connected knowledge base or document repository
Not for building or populating a knowledge base — use KnowledgeBaseBuilder
Cannot search the public web — use WebResearchSummarizer
skillBody: Parse and embed the search query
Run semantic search over knowledge base
Return cited answer with source references

name: DocumentSummarizer
description: Produces concise, structured summaries of long documents, reports, or articles. Supports key-point extraction, executive summaries, and custom summary formats (bullets, narrative, TLDR).
triggerConditions: User provides a long document and wants it condensed
User asks for a TLDR or executive summary of a document
User wants key points extracted from a lengthy report
examples: Summarize this 40-page strategy document in 5 bullet points
Give me a TLDR of this research report
Write an executive summary of this annual report
limitations: Not for deep analysis of academic papers — use AcademicPaperAnalyzer
Not for extracting structured data from invoices or forms
Should not replace full document reading for legal or compliance review
skillBody: Load and chunk the input document
Identify main arguments and supporting points

name: SOPGenerator
description: Creates Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) documents from process descriptions, interviews, or existing notes. Produces step-by-step procedures with decision points, roles, and compliance notes.
triggerConditions: User wants to document a process as an SOP
User describes a workflow and wants it formalized
User asks for a step-by-step procedure document
examples: Write an SOP for our employee onboarding process
Turn this process description into a formal SOP document
Create a step-by-step procedure for handling customer escalations
limitations: Not for general document creation — use WordDocumentCreator
Not for project planning — use ProjectPlanGenerator
Should not replace domain-expert review for safety-critical SOPs
skillBody: Identify roles, decision points, and exceptions
Structure as numbered steps with sub-steps
Add compliance and safety notes where relevant
Format and export as a professional SOP document

name: ContentWriter
description: Creates original long-form written content including blog posts, articles, LinkedIn posts, social media copy, product descriptions, and marketing copy. Adapts tone, style, and length to platform and audience.
triggerConditions: User wants to create marketing, editorial, or social content
User asks for a blog post, article, or social media copy
User needs written content for a specific audience or channel
examples: Write a 1,000-word blog post on the future of remote work
Create 5 LinkedIn post variations for our product launch
Write a product description for our new analytics dashboard
limitations: Not for drafting formal emails — use EmailDraftComposer
Not for technical documentation — use SOPGenerator or WordDocumentCreator
Should not be selected for academic writing or citations
skillBody: Clarify topic, audience, tone, and length
Draft structured content with intro, body, and conclusion
Optimize for SEO or platform if specified

name: ToneRewriter
description: Rewrites existing text in a specified tone or style (formal, casual, assertive, empathetic, persuasive, simplified). Preserves original meaning while adapting register, vocabulary, and sentence structure.
triggerConditions: User provides text and asks for it to be rewritten in a different tone
User wants to simplify, formalize, or energize existing content
User asks to adapt copy for a different audience
examples: Rewrite this email to sound more empathetic and less blunt
Make this technical paragraph easier to understand for a non-technical audience
Rewrite this blog post intro to be more punchy and engaging
limitations: Not for generating new content from scratch — use ContentWriter
Not for translating to another language — use LanguageTranslator
Should not be used for legally binding documents without expert review
skillBody: Parse original text and identify current tone
Adjust vocabulary, sentence structure, and register
Preserve original meaning and key information
Return rewritten text with tone applied

name: LanguageTranslator
description: Translates text or documents between languages while preserving meaning, tone, and formatting. Supports over 50 languages and handles idiomatic expressions, domain-specific terminology, and cultural nuance.
triggerConditions: User wants text translated into another language
User provides content in one language and asks for it in another
User wants to localize a document or message
examples: Translate this contract summary from English to Spanish
Convert this product description into French and German
Translate this customer support email from Japanese to English
limitations: Not for tone rewriting in the same language — use ToneRewriter
Not for legal or certified translation requiring human translators
Complex idiomatic content may require human review
skillBody: Detect source language if not specified
Return translated content in target language

name: DataPipelineBuilder
description: Designs and generates code for data pipelines including ETL workflows, data ingestion scripts, transformation logic, and scheduling configurations. Supports Python, SQL, and common orchestration frameworks.
triggerConditions: User wants to build a data pipeline or ETL workflow
User needs to move or transform data between systems
User asks for an ingestion or transformation script
examples: Build a Python ETL pipeline to move data from PostgreSQL to BigQuery daily
Create a data ingestion script for our S3 to Snowflake pipeline
Write a transformation job to normalize this raw events table
limitations: Not for executing code — use CodeExecutor
Not for querying databases directly — use SQLQueryRunner
Not for analyzing data — use SpreadsheetAnalyzer or SQLQueryRunner
skillBody: Understand source, target, and transformation requirements
Generate extraction, transformation, and loading code
Return complete pipeline code or DAG definition

name: UserStoryWriter
description: Converts product ideas, feature requests, or requirements into well-formed user stories following the standard 'As a [user], I want [goal], so that [benefit]' format. Includes acceptance criteria and story point estimates.
triggerConditions: User wants to write user stories for a product feature
User has a feature idea and wants it broken into stories
User asks for acceptance criteria for a requirement
examples: Write user stories for a password reset feature
Convert this feature spec into 5 user stories with acceptance criteria
Break down the shopping cart feature into user stories for the sprint
limitations: Not for creating full project plans — use ProjectPlanGenerator
Not for managing or tracking tasks in a tool — use TaskManager
Not for technical specification documents — use WordDocumentCreator
skillBody: Define measurable acceptance criteria for each story

name: WebSearchFetcher
description: Performs a raw web search using a text query or URL and returns unprocessed results including page URLs, document URLs (PDFs, docs), and raw extracted text from each result page. Does not summarize or synthesize — returns raw source material for downstream processing.
triggerConditions: User wants raw web search results without summarization
User provides a URL and wants its raw content fetched
User wants to see source text directly from a website
User needs a list of URLs and their unprocessed page content
User explicitly asks to fetch or scrape web content
examples: Fetch the raw content of this URL: https://example.com/article
Search for 'LangChain documentation embeddings' and return the raw results
Get me the raw text from the top 5 results for this query
Fetch the document at this PDF URL and return its raw text
Scrape this webpage and give me the raw HTML text
limitations: Does not summarize or synthesize results — use WebResearchSummarizer for that
Cannot access pages behind authentication or paywalls
Not suitable for academic paper analysis — use AcademicPaperAnalyzer
May return noisy or unstructured content depending on the source website
Not intended for fact-checking — use FactChecker for that
skillBody: Accept a text query or direct URL as input
Execute web search or HTTP fetch against the target URL
Extract raw text content from each result page
Identify and collect document URLs (PDFs, DOCX, etc.) found in results
Return structured list of results with URL, document URL if present, and raw extracted text
